newsitem.title: UK: Russia repeats it not responsible for Tsarist debt.
newsitem.headline: Russia repeats it not responsible for Tsarist debt.

text.p: The Russian government, trying to tap international capital markets for the first time since the 1917 revolution, reiterated on Friday that was not responsible for old Tsarist bonds.

"Russia has never declared responsibility for the debt issued during the Tsarist period," Russian Finance Minister Alexander Livshits told reporters in London, where he is promoting the country's first sovereign bond issue in more than 80 years.
Mainly French holders of Tsarist-era bonds say Moscow, which refused to honour the debt when the Bolsheviks took over in 1917, owes them $30 billion.
Russia is currently in talks with the French government on the issue, but Livshits said this was over "mutual claims" only.
"That is why holders of the bonds in France have to go to the French government. It is a completely internal matter," he said.
